title: Implementation of quantum gates by Floquet analysis of kicked quantum system
authors: Andrea De Luca, Carola Ciaramelletti, Simone Paganelli
abstract: Precise control of multi-qubit architectures remains a critical bottleneck in superconducting quantum processors. In this work, we investigate the synthesis of high-fidelity quantum operations and state transfer protocols within an extended superconducting linear chain, scaling from three to seven sites. Using Floquet theory, we model the periodic drive as a train of delta-like pulses, mapping the quantum control problem onto quasi-energy resonance conditions. Combining the Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff expansion with Floquet spectral decomposition, we analytically identify optimal driving parameters, refined via the Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy (CMA-ES). In the three-qubit architecture, this enables high-fidelity synthesis of the iSWAP gate. Extending to a seven-site chain, we implement periodic trains of finite-width Gaussian pulses to activate distinct double-excitation transport channels with ultra-short gate durations t_gate (~170 ns). This achieves a clear scale separation from energy-relaxation times (T1) typical of fixed-frequency transmon devices with tunable couplers, such as IBM Quantum hardware. Finally, we benchmark stability under realistic imperfections, revealing a heightened sensitivity to static parameter disorder at the sub-percent level (eta ~ 10^-3) driven by spectral crowding, and discuss how closed-loop topologies could mitigate this constraint. This framework bridges time-periodic control theory and practical quantum gate engineering.
summary: This paper details a method to implement high-fidelity quantum gates in superconducting qubit arrays by utilizing Floquet engineering with periodic driving pulses. By mapping the problem to quasi-energy resonance conditions and optimizing parameters, the authors achieve robust gate operations that scale to larger systems. This framework provides a powerful theoretical tool for advancing practical quantum hardware control.
main_problem: The core challenge is achieving high-fidelity quantum gate operations and state transfer protocols in superconducting multi-qubit processors.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated high-fidelity iSWAP gate synthesis in a three-qubit system and extended the protocol to a seven-site chain using periodic Gaussian driving pulses.
method: The work employs Floquet theory to analyze the time-periodic Hamiltonian, mapping the control problem onto quasi-energy resonance conditions, which are then optimized using CMA-ES.
model_or_system: The system is an extended superconducting linear chain of transmon qubits (scaling from three to seven sites), modeled by a time-dependent Hamiltonian driven by periodic pulses.
key_observables: Gate fidelity ($F_{i	o f}$), quasi-energy spectrum, and the ability to achieve clear scale separation from energy-relaxation times ($T_1$).
important_parameters: Kick strength ($\lambda$), driving period ($T$), static coupling strengths ($g_1, g_2$), and the disorder parameter ($\eta \sim 10^{-3}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis initially uses the idealized delta-like pulse model, but extends to finite-width Gaussian pulses; stability is benchmarked against static parameter disorder.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the circuit scheme, the poor performance of the undriven system, and the optimized, high-fidelity state transfer achieved via Floquet driving.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical system and Hamiltonian, applying Floquet theory to derive the stroboscopic evolution operator, optimizing parameters via CMA-ES to achieve resonance, and finally benchmarking the resulting gate fidelity against realistic hardware imperfections.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges advanced time-periodic control theory (Floquet engineering) with the practical engineering challenges of superconducting quantum hardware, providing concrete, scalable protocols for quantum computation.
